reviews.summary: The logging half of the row, and only that half. `agents/core/security/log_redaction.py` adds `SecretRedactionFilter`, a `logging.Filter` that runs every record's message and its `args` through `SecretScanner.redact` before a handler can write it. The enable flag is snapshotted at import, so an agent-authored mid-session write to `JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION` cannot turn it off — Hermes's `_REDACT_ENABLED` rule, ported deliberately. A cheap length/substring pre-check runs before any regex (≈8.75 µs per clean record, ~1.9× faster than the full scan; the builder's report said 17.22 µs and ~2.1×, which did not reproduce and is corrected here). `setup_logging()` installs it. **Two majors found by an independent review and fixed before landing:** the module's own docstring tripped the AUD-14 raw-env-read ratchet — the prose contained a literal `os.environ[...]` subscript and the ratchet greps file text line by line, so `tests/test_o26_p2_env_config.py` was RED in the delivered tree; and `install_log_redaction()` walked only the root logger's handlers, while `uvicorn` and `uvicorn.access` set `propagate=False` and own theirs, so the production HTTP server's own access and error logs — the ones that carry an `Authorization` header — were structurally unreachable. `install_log_redaction_everywhere()` now covers every handler owned by any logger in `logging.Logger.manager`, and a test drives a real uvicorn `dictConfig` and asserts a key in an access line is masked. Three minors fixed with it: the length floor was defeated by an extra pattern whose NAME collided with a built-in (it now matches by regex SHAPE, one-to-one, and fails closed on any mismatch); an ordinary `%`-format bug was being swallowed into a bare `[redaction-unavailable]` instead of logging's loud diagnostic (now `[log-format-error]` with the message, args and exception, all scanned first); and the test fixture destroyed an ambient `JARVIS_LOG_FILE` for the rest of the session. 47 tests, each fix red-proofed by neutering it. **Follow-up in the same PR:** the blocking bandit gate flagged both swallowed exceptions as NEW findings. Only the filter's last-ditch blank was suppressed (`# nosec B110`, with its reason); `_cover`'s per-handler swallow became a counted, warned coverage figure and `_managed_loggers`' registry-walk failure became a warning, closing the gap this row disclosed. 52 tests at landing. **#1177 (2026-09-19) closed a log-integrity hole inside this same control, re-assessed here rather than refreshed:** the in-place path used to give up and flatten the record to `msg`/`()` whenever a secret straddled the boundary between the format string and an argument ("correctness beats shape"), and flattening is exactly what DELETES a uvicorn access line — `AccessFormatter` unpacks five `record.args`, raises on an empty tuple, and `Handler.handleError` swallows it. `password_assignment`'s `\s*[=:]\s*` jumps the space uvicorn's `'%s - "%s %s HTTP/%s" %d'` puts between the request path and `HTTP/`, so `/login?pwd=` is inert on its own — 11 characters, so the 10-char floor does not even apply; `password_assignment` needs at least six unquoted (four quoted) non-space characters after the separator and the bare argument has none — and a match once rendered: any unauthenticated client could erase its own access-log entry by appending `?pwd=` to a path. `SecretRedactionFilter._mask_joined_args` now replaces whole arguments — one at a time first, then cumulatively for a secret assembled from several — the cumulative pass can also mask an innocent argument that sits between two culprits (`"%s HTTP/%s and %s HTTP/%s"` with two `?pwd=` paths loses the `1.1` between them): over-redaction, never a leak, and the arity still holds — — until the re-rendered line is scanner-clean, keeping the tuple's arity, putting an argument back when its conversion refuses the mask (uvicorn's `%d` status code stays an int), and naming the mask after the pattern the scanner reports, `[REDACTED:straddling_secret]` when it cannot. Flattening survives only for a straddle no masking can clean, i.e. the secret sits in the format string itself (`pwd=%s`). Seven tests were added — four of them through uvicorn's real `dictConfig` plus `setup_logging()`, asserting the access line for `/login?pwd=`, `/admin?password=`, `/x?passwd:` and `/z?api_key="12345678` survives with the straddling text gone (three are `password_assignment` straddles; `/z?api_key="12345678` is `generic_api_key` matching `api_key="12345678 HTTP/1.1"`, the access line's own closing quote completing the quoted value) and the client, verb and status kept — and the earlier straddle test was inverted to assert `args == ("[REDACTED:anthropic_key]",)` instead of `()`. `agents/core/log.py` did not change and still installs the filter from `setup_logging()`. `tests/test_log_redaction.py` collects 64 tests, all green on 2026-09-19. Nothing in #1177 touches the other six paths the row names; the still-owed list below stands.
reviews.remaining: This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies `redact.py` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a `cat .env` from `terminal_run` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning `[redaction-unavailable]` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID `«redacted:ghp_…»` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), `code_file=True` sparing source constants, `_mask_control_split_tokens()` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared `.env` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose `addFilter` fails is counted and published through `uncovered_handler_count()` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a `loggerDict` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (`# nosec B110`), where a `logging.Filter` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. `install_log_redaction()` remains exported although the `everywhere` variant is what production uses. **A later slice's full-suite run surfaced one more thing about this control, recorded here rather than fixed:** the scanner's `high_entropy_secret` pattern matches an ordinary filesystem path. Under `-n auto --dist loadfile` a warning naming a pytest tmp file arrived as `truncated: [REDACTED:high_entropy_secret].md`, which is what a real operator would see when a log line names a file with a long random-looking segment — a debuggability cost the module docstring already warns about in general terms, now with a concrete case. Separately, `setup_logging()` installs the filter on every handler of every logger and nothing took it back off, so every later test on the same xdist worker ran under a live redactor. The installer is PRODUCTION code, not the tests: `agents/run.py` calls `setup_logging()` at module level, so importing it installs the filter during pytest COLLECTION — before any fixture runs — and eight test files import it; `agents/web.py` calls it from the FastAPI lifespan, so any test that drives the app installs it again; five test files call it directly on top of that. There is no list of leaking files to fix. The cleanup therefore lives in `tests/conftest.py` as an autouse fixture that strips unconditionally BEFORE each test as well as after — a snapshot-and-restore fixture, which is what the two neighbouring isolation fixtures do and what this was first written as, treats a collection-time install as pre-existing and preserves it for the life of the worker. That version went green locally and RED in CI on exactly the test it was meant to fix. The first attempt at it matched by `isinstance` and silently did nothing: `agents/` is on `sys.path`, so `core.security.log_redaction` and `agents.core.security.log_redaction` are two module objects over this one file with two distinct `SecretRedactionFilter` classes, and the root handler was carrying the other one. The match is by class name now, and four paired tests pin both halves — including the alternate import path, which is the case the first attempt missed.

reviews.summary: **Gap (a) of four, plus the row's `chmod 0600 atomic writes` clause.** Both pairing credentials stop being written in the clear: `SenderPairing._code` becomes `_code_hash`, and each deeplink entry moves from being keyed by its raw token to being keyed by an opaque 8-byte id with the token's salted digest inside the entry. Verification hashes the candidate and `hmac.compare_digest`s two fixed-length hex digests, so neither the length nor any prefix of the stored credential leaks and the deeplink failure reasons stay indistinguishable. A one-time migration accepts a pre-H497 plaintext file, rehashes it in memory and rewrites it, preserving each link's channel, `created_at` and `expires_at` — an upgrade never locks the owner out nor resurrects a spent link. `_digest` encodes with `surrogatepass` so a lone surrogate (from a hand-edited store, or from the body of the one pairing route a stranger is meant to reach) misses instead of raising. `atomic_write_json` lands every JsonStore file owner-only. **The review found three false claims and all three are corrected — two of them by changing the code rather than the prose.** (1) The module docstring said the store "holds nothing that can pair anybody". True of a 192-bit deeplink token; **false of the pairing code**, which is whatever the owner typed: a four-digit code was recovered from the file by exhausting 10,000 candidates in **0.006 s** and then used to pair. The code is now stretched with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 240,000 rounds, `kdf` and `rounds` stored beside each digest so raising the count later cannot lock an owner out, and a record written by the first cut is upgraded in place on the next successful pair — the one moment the plaintext is in hand — while a FAILED guess leaves it untouched. The deeplink token stays on plain SHA-256, deliberately: `redeem_deeplink` hashes once per outstanding link, so a slow hash there is a CPU lever for any stranger sending `/start junk`, and at 192 bits there is nothing for stretching to buy. (2) The salt comment defended leaving the code unstretched by pointing at the store-wide guess budget — an ONLINE control held in memory, which has no bearing on an attacker who has read the file, the exact threat at-rest hashing answers. Rewritten to say what stretching does and does not promise. (3) `atomic_write_json` claimed its chmod-before-replace ordering left no readable window. It left a shorter one: `write_text` creates the tmp at `0o666 & ~umask` and the whole payload is in it before the chmod runs. The payload now goes through a descriptor opened 0600, so the window is actually closed — pinned by a test that neutralises `os.chmod` and still requires 0600.
reviews.remaining: **The row names four hardening gaps and this closes (a) only.** Still outstanding, from the row itself: (b) *no lockout after N failed attempts* — the row wants a 1 h lockout after 5 failed approvals, checked BEFORE the pending lookup so a code already in flight cannot be brute-forced past it; there is still only a rate limit and an in-memory guess budget, both of which reset on restart. (c) *revocation is not verified to reach live adapters* — `revoke_deeplinks()` and `unpair()` clear the store only, nothing touches a running Telegram or Slack adapter, and no test says it does. (d) *no admin-vs-user command split on channels*, so any paired sender gets every command; the row wants a split with an always-allowed floor of `{help, whoami}`. **Unaddressed from the Hermes column:** pairing-code GENERATION (8 characters from a 32-char unambiguous alphabet via `secrets.choice`) and the code's 1 h TTL — the code here never expires; "max 3 pending per platform" (the store bounds 200 globally); "1 request per user per 10 min" (it is 5); `unauthorized_dm_behavior` treating inbox-shaped platforms differently from chat-shaped ones; and the ordered authorization union (allow-all flag → pairing approvals → per-platform allowlist → global allowlist → global allow-all → default DENY), which is still an ad-hoc sequence in `is_allowed`/`gate_inbound`. **And the honest limit on what this slice does close.** Stretching is a work factor, not a wall: it multiplies the cost of every candidate by the round count and nothing more. A four-digit code goes from milliseconds to minutes; an eight-character mixed-alphabet code becomes infeasible. **Nothing enforces a floor on what the owner types** — `PairingCodeBody` caps the length at 128 and sets no minimum — and generating the code for them is the row's own prescription and is not implemented. Until it is, the at-rest guarantee for the code is exactly as strong as the owner's choice, and the module says so in those words rather than the ones it used to.

reviews.summary: **`JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE` flips from opt-in to default-on**, so a spawned stdio MCP server is handed the `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` baseline plus its own `env` instead of `os.environ.copy()` — API keys, tokens, proxies and every `JARVIS_*` setting withheld. A second flag, `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV`, is the owner-reachable migration remedy: a comma-separated list of host variable names that pass the baseline even when `_SECRET_LIKE` matches them. `_merged_env()` emits one INFO line per connect counting host values the child does not receive, carrying **no variable name and no value**. `GET /api/admin/mcp` rows gain `env_baseline`. And Nerva's own WorldView MCP server is handed its `WORLDVIEW_API_URL`, which the flip would otherwise have silently replaced with the built-in `http://localhost:4000`. **The review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed.** **(1)** `routers/mcp.py` asserted an invariant the code did not hold: the comment said a row that spawns no subprocess reports `None` "rather than a badge it has not earned" and enumerated two cases. A third exists and is the only one an owner can create today — `POST /api/admin/mcp` does no command validation, so a row with a whitespace-only command or a shell metacharacter persists, and `connect()` answers `unsafe_command` from `_command_argv()` **before** `create_subprocess_exec`. Such a row reported `env_baseline: true` for a child that never existed; the row now calls the same `_command_argv()` `connect` does, so the two cannot disagree, and the guard test carries both spellings. **(2)** `BACKLOG.md` still shipped the pre-flip claim and therefore stated the OPPOSITE of the code — "opt-in, default-off … keeps working until the owner opts in" — in the one file `CLAUDE.md` tells a reader to query for what is delivered. That is exactly the misreading the slice's own documentation work exists to prevent. Corrected, and `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` now covers BACKLOG.md too, including a check that the "opt-in, default-off" wording is gone. Two wording corrections went with them: the `env_baseline` field describes the live FLAG, i.e. the posture for the NEXT spawn, not the environment the running child holds (`_merged_env()` runs once at connect, the row is read per request); and the migration note steered the reader at auth failures only, when the flip also withholds `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` — plumbing whose absence produces an ImportError, a hang or a connect timeout, nothing resembling an auth error.
reviews.remaining: **The documented per-server `env` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.** `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field, `POST /api/admin/mcp` drops the key (pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`), and neither `to_config` nor `load_from_config` writes or reads one. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the **host-wide** `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV`, which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` §P28.3 with both options. **Related and also owner-level:** `XAUTHORITY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are both on `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST`, and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. **And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:** this is **defence in depth, not a security boundary**. The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of `/proc/<ppid>/environ`. What the baseline buys is that a *careless* or *curious* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's `JARVIS_*` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise. **Unaddressed from the row:** there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary, and `POST /api/admin/mcp` still accepts any command string. This slice hardens what the child *receives*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to *be*.

reviews.summary: **The write half, as a generic mechanism rather than a special case.** `agents/core/tool_rpc.py` gains a registrar-owned *call classifier*: a gated tool may register a pure function over one call's args returning bounded labels. `handle()` stamps them onto the durable approval card's payload and appends the notice to the card title; `execute()` re-derives them from the args about to run and refuses with `approval_class_mismatch` unless the approved card carried the same `class` — so a card approved as a scratch note cannot be redeemed against a write to SOUL.md. `_classify` fails closed (a raising, non-Mapping, over-long or non-alphanumeric result refuses the call rather than letting it through unlabelled) and strips the reserved `tool`/`args`/`target` keys so labels cannot rewrite the card's identity. `agents/core/file_tools.py` registers `FileTools.classify_mutation` for `file_write` and `file_delete`, matches on the BASENAME in any directory inside the roots (an instruction file is wherever the harness that reads it looks — `_load_soul` alone searches three), carries a `steers_future_runs` flag into the kernel Action payload, and adds a secondary floor in `_mutate`. A sandboxed script cannot label its own write nor strip the label off one: the classifier is registrar-owned and `handle()` returns `approval_required` before the handler is ever reached. **The review found one major and it is fixed here.** The roster omitted `HEARTBEAT.md` and `HEARTBEAT.local.md` — the files in this repo that *literally* schedule future runs: `core/heartbeat.py` scans every agent directory for them, prefers the gitignored `.local` overlay exactly as `SOUL.local.md` does, and turns what it finds into cron-scheduled agent runs. Reproduced against a real `ToolRPCServer`: a write to `HEARTBEAT.local.md` produced `class=None` and the generic title "Tool 'file_write' via RPC" — a card byte-identical to a write to a scratch note, for an action that installs a cron expression driving every later run. Both names are in the class now, and the roster is pinned against `heartbeat.py`'s own source rather than restated, so a loader that learns a new name fails the test instead of silently escaping the class. The exact-set pin beside it was tightened, not loosened. **Widened by #1177 (the #1161–#1174 adversarial review) — same mechanism, larger class, re-assessed here.** The roster is now `INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES` (`soul.md`, `agents.md`, `claude.md`, `gemini.md`, `.cursorrules`, `heartbeat.md`) and every `.md` name's gitignored `.local` overlay is *derived* by `_local_overlay` into `INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES` (eleven names) instead of being spelled out by hand — which is what brought `CLAUDE.local.md` / `AGENTS.local.md` / `GEMINI.local.md` into the class; the first cut listed only the SOUL and HEARTBEAT overlays, so a `CLAUDE.local.md` write — same harness, same authority, and it wins over the committed file — asked with the title of a scratch note. `looks_instruction_name` now also matches by extension through `INSTRUCTION_FILE_SUFFIXES = (".mdc",)`, so Cursor's freely-named `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files, the format that superseded `.cursorrules`, are in the class as well. `classify_mutation`, the `steers_future_runs` flag, `_authorize`, the `_mutate` floor and `register_file_tools` are unchanged, and `tool_rpc.py` is byte-identical. Tests: `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_floor.py` (44) pins both sets exactly (the six base names and the eleven derived ones), derives the overlay requirement from the roster in `test_every_name_in_the_roster_brings_its_local_overlay` so a name added later brings its overlay or fails, keeps the heartbeat.py-derived pin, and exercises `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` through `write_file` with the kernel off; `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_class_toolrpc.py` (18) proves the durable card for `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` carries `class=agent_instructions` and the notice in its title, and that nothing reaches disk before approval.
reviews.remaining: **The read half is now half there, and by another row's hand — so the row stays partial.** H506 requires the same file class to be scanned at context-load time for injection payloads — ignore-prior-instructions, hidden HTML comments, secret-reading and curl-exfil shapes, zero-width and bidi characters — with a positive match replaced by `[BLOCKED: … Content not loaded.]`. Since H387 (#1173, which predates #1177) `Agent._load_soul` no longer passes SOUL.md through unscanned: `_scan_soul_body` runs `detect_injection` per line over a `strip_format_chars` copy (the original line is kept), decodes invisible TAG characters before scanning, replaces each flagged line with a `[BLOCKED: line N of SOUL.md …]` stub, drops the whole body for `_blocked_soul_body` above `_SOUL_BLOCK_RATIO`, and reports `flags`/`blocked` to the HUD. **#1177 touched this half without saying so, and not for the better.** `agents/core/security/quarantine.py` — the read-side path this row's own evidence names — now documents that scanning only the stripped copy is weaker than scanning raw and stripped (a deletion destroys a match as readily as it uncovers one: 'You are now<U+200B>in developer mode' supplies the pattern's word boundary with the zero-width space itself), adds `detect_injection_normalized` as the union scan, and wires it into `skills/loader.py` only. `_scan_soul_body` was left on `detect_injection(strip_format_chars(line))`, so at 494a13b2 that ZWS line reaches the system prompt unflagged (flags == [], blocked False) while `detect_injection_normalized` flags it; and because #1177 also widened `strip_format_chars` to C0/C1 controls, Mn and the Hangul fillers, a persona line 'You are now<U+0007>in developer mode.' that the SOUL scan flagged at 1c5054ea is unflagged at 494a13b2. `tests/test_soul_injection_guard.py` (37) pins neither case. The fix is one call-site change plus a test pinning both spellings, and it belongs to H387's evidence, not this row's — but a reader of this row must not take the SOUL scan as covering the zero-width shapes the Hermes text lists. That covers SOUL.md / SOUL.local.md only. `core/heartbeat.py` still turns HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md into cron-scheduled runs with no injection scan at all, and AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / `.cursorrules` / `*.mdc` are read by the external harnesses rather than by Nerva — so "the same file class on the way in" is not met, and the H387 evidence is pinned on that row, not this one, so this row does not count it. Three smaller deviations, named rather than smoothed over. The row's *"fails closed on a config read error"* clause has no analogue, because the roster is a hard-coded frozenset (`INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES` plus its derived overlays and the `.mdc` suffix) with no config to read — arguably stronger, but nobody has adjudicated the substitution. The row's `allow_session=False` (each write re-asks) holds only *incidentally*: every gated toolrpc call still hard-codes `autonomy_level="ask"` and `govern_enqueue` takes the stricter of caller and policy, so no `--yolo` path can auto-approve one today — but nothing pins it, so a future policy change that weakened gated toolrpc intake would turn no H506 test red. And the class covers `file_write`/`file_delete` only: `looks_instruction_name` has no consumer outside `file_tools.py`, so any other way an instruction file could be written — the terminal contract (#1177 hardened it without consulting this class), the skill importer, the desktop operator — is outside it entirely. **One thing the review checked and could not close, stated as unchecked rather than as verified:** the queue path carries the notice untruncated (`TaskQueue.enqueue` stores the title as given and `govern_enqueue` passes it through), but whether the Telegram decision card and the HUD decision inbox render that title verbatim to the owner's eyes is untested by this slice. The notice is the whole point of the class, so the last hop being unproven is worth a reader knowing. Finally, `_mutate`'s floor is deliberately weaker than `skill.install`'s permanent one: it is lifted by a caller-supplied `approved=True`, and the shipped ToolRPC path passes it by design — defence-in-depth for the next direct caller, not the production gate.

reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:626, applied at :679-680), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:655-657 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin `plugin.egress` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul.

H557 is PARTIAL, not missing and not equivalent. The 2026-09-07 verdict is stale on one half and still correct on the other; the overnight triage's "already equivalent" is wrong.

SHIPPED (the row's rationale half). The name-collision correctness bug is fixed and tested: agents/core/mcp/client.py:566-594 `MCPManager._resolve` accepts a bare tool name only when exactly one server offers it and otherwise returns `{"error": "ambiguous_tool", "servers": [...]}`; `server/tool` or an explicit `server=` pins the server; `find_tool` (client.py:597) and `call_tool` (client.py:606) both route through it; `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:230-233) is the `server/tool` form. tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-73 proves first-wins is gone (3 tests, passing). This is a genuine different-spelling equivalent of Hermes' disambiguation property, so `missing` under-reports the row.

NOT SHIPPED (the row's headline half). There is no `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` equivalent. agents/core/mcp/client.py:402-417 `_list_tools` still stores `t.get("inputSchema", {})` verbatim (client.py:410) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (client.py:220) with zero repair — the 2026-09-07 evidence sentence is still literally true. Nerva repairs at the dialect boundary instead, and only for ONE of four providers: agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-437 `gemini_schema` covers Hermes' `required`-pruning (:423-427) and missing-`type` coercion (:419, :427), and :441-452 avoids the empty-OBJECT 400. The Anthropic path (tool_dialects.py:147-151) and both OpenAI paths (tool_protocol.py:19-27 `as_openai`, responses.py:72-81) pass `input_schema` through byte-for-byte. Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path: I ran the code and confirmed `gemini_schema({"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null})` → `{"default": null, "anyOf": [{"type":"string"}, {}]}` (the Pydantic null branch is not collapsed, it degenerates to an empty schema), and `{"definitions":{"Node":…},"properties":{"node":{"$ref":"#/definitions/Node"}}}` → `{"properties":{"node":{}}}` (draft-07 `definitions`/`$ref` are not promoted to `$defs`, the referenced shape is silently deleted). No name sanitization exists anywhere: `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` is empty, and `qualified_name`'s `/` is not a legal provider function-name character.

ON REACHABILITY. The triage is right that this is currently unreachable from a model: `MCPManager.get_tools()` (client.py:560-564) has zero callers in the whole repo, `MCPTool.input_schema` is read nowhere outside its constructor, and agents/core/routers/mcp.py:71-79 and :193-194 expose only name/description/read_only to the HUD, never the schema. But the triage's grep was scoped wrong and missed a real production consumer of the dispatch path: agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:141 calls `self.mcp.call_tool(tool, mcp_args)` by bare name (it lives inside agents/core/mcp/, which their grep excluded). So `_resolve` is not dead code, and its bare-name path is live today.

Unreachability is a reason the remaining work is small and belongs inside the bridge PR — it is not a reason to record the row as done. Six of Hermes' nine clauses are unsatisfied or satisfied on only one of four provider paths, and no test anywhere exercises repair of a third-party `inputSchema`. Recording `equivalent` would put a false claim on a public status page; `partial` with a named remainder is the honest row.
reviews.remaining: No provider-agnostic repair of a third-party MCP server's JSON Schema exists. (1) `agents/core/mcp/client.py:402-417` `_list_tools` still stores `inputSchema` verbatim (`:410`); add a `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` applied at registration. (2) Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path, verified by running the code: draft-07 `definitions`/`#/definitions/...` are never promoted to `$defs`/`#/$defs/...` (and `gemini_schema` silently reduces a `$ref` property to `{}`, deleting the shape), and a Pydantic nullable union `anyOf:[{...},{"type":"null"}], default:null` is never collapsed to its non-null branch (`gemini_schema` yields `anyOf:[{"type":"string"},{}]` with `default:null` retained — the exact shape Anthropic 400s on). (3) The three repairs that do exist (`required` pruned to declared names, missing `type` coerced, empty-OBJECT avoided) live only in `agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-452` and therefore apply to Gemini alone; `anthropic_tools` (tool_dialects.py:147-151), `ToolSpec.as_openai` (tool_protocol.py:19-27) and the Responses payload (responses.py:72-81) pass `input_schema` through unrepaired. (4) No name sanitization or provider-legal prefixing: `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:230-233) is `server/tool`, whose `/` is outside the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` function-name charset both Anthropic and OpenAI enforce, and nothing replaces characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` returns nothing. (5) The row's security property — a third-party tool shadowing a built-in governed tool name — is unaddressed: `_resolve` disambiguates only among MCP servers, never against the agent tool registry. (6) No test covers any of this; `grep -rln "gemini_schema" tests/` returns only tests/test_cloud_tool_turns.py, and nothing tests `MCPTool.input_schema`. All of the above is currently unreachable by a model because no MCP-client -> tool-registry bridge exists (`MCPManager.get_tools()` has zero callers repo-wide), so the normalizer plus its tests should land inside whichever PR first offers MCP client tools to the model, not as a standalone pure function.

reviews.summary: K2/K3 now include a production detached Docker worker over run-to-completion CLI calls, with a private size-limited container mailbox, bounded response packets/backpressure, ready handshake, cell nonces, asynchronous liveness monitoring, and kill/reset/cancel lifecycle. Each cell still crosses the current host authorization and ToolCallBroker. Only a proved pre-dispatch startup refusal permits explicit isolated per-call fallback; dispatched/ambiguous cells never retry. Python cell stdout/stderr streams now reach existing ToolResultStore spills before preview truncation, retaining the middle without unbounded worker buffers. Session tool-RPC uses directory-pinned no-follow I/O and random cell directories, closing a reproduced host-write symlink issue. Existing opt-in settings and digest-pinned Docker isolation remain. Independent-review repairs recheck e-stop/expiry and authorization inside fallback dispatch, retain unconfirmed removals as quarantined records with retryable operator reset, validate hostile stream labels, and keep deadline/stop monitoring independent of awaited tool calls. Late broker replies cannot write after cancellation; old-cell cleanup cannot destroy a replacement kernel. Native macOS and Linux real-Docker containment are now verified. The host CLI and local Unix endpoint are frozen; private CLI configuration prevents operator proxy credentials reaching the worker, including after context changes.
reviews.remaining: Generic SSH, Modal and remote TLS provisioning remain unsupported and require an explicitly isolated governed transport design. Docker selection currently supports local Unix endpoints. Correlation tokens/nonces reject stale frames but cannot attest output against Python introspection inside the same worker; authorization is enforced by the host broker. Full spills cover redirected Python stdout/stderr, not deliberate native-fd bypasses. Production deployment evidence is separate from these real-container tests.

reviews.summary: Durable session birth is resolved through an immutable, generation-checked continuation root. Explicit owner-created child sessions carry bounded retained context and root birth through multiple generations, text/stream/process entrypoints and restart without switching the shared default. SQLite atomically commits child identity, seed, lineage and initial clock; idempotent request receipts resolve retries. Corrupt newer snapshots, reused identities and failed recovery stop dispatch or writes instead of silently replacing context. Accepted history/tool compaction alone advances the durable rebuild clock through compare-and-swap; request snapshots preserve same-day prefix bytes, reject late inherited commits, and add the trusted current-date line only when rebuild and root-birth days differ. Production rendering resolves explicit TZ or existing local IANA discovery and uses historical/current DST rules with an explicit UTC offset. Unknown birth is omitted; invalid or unavailable zone discovery preserves truthful offset-only rendering rather than inventing an IANA name. Independent actual-route, Agent, restart, concurrency, cancellation, failed-resume and observe-only regressions support the full frozen clock contract. This is code-equivalence, not a live-provider claim; ordinary subsequent JSON persistence remains best effort and turn leases are process-local.

Both refreshes from Hermes's row exist (`agents/core/session_refresh.py`, the parked mechanism commit 89b53e85 cherry-picked unchanged) and are now wired at Nerva's two compaction boundaries, each failing in its own direction. **Nerva is turn-based, so most of the row was already true between turns and is pinned as such**: `Orchestrator._prompt_context` reads the skills catalog per turn, the plugin block is rendered per turn, and `AgentToolRuntime._run_loop` resolves ToolRPC → capability registry → tool profile at the top of every run (`test_between_turns_the_offer_was_already_live`). Two things were not live. **(1) The system prompt.** `Agent._load_soul` ran once in `__init__` and `orchestrator.py` sent `agent.soul["content"]` for the life of the process, so a persona edited or quarantined mid-session needed a restart. `Agent._read_soul` is now the one builder (same file resolution, same H387 scan, same cap) behind both `_load_soul` and the new `Agent.refresh_soul`, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (orchestrator.py, a module function so the bare-stub tests of that path keep working) calls it for every agent from `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` — after the clock CAS, never before it — through `session_refresh.refresh_prompt`: the keep path is byte equality of the builder's output (a rewrite of the same bytes leaves the very dict the HUD reports untouched), a builder that throws or a file absent for the instant of an editor's rename keeps the last-good bytes (fails OPEN), and a scan verdict is not a failure — a persona that is now mostly injection is dropped exactly as a restart would drop it. **(2) The tool set inside one turn.** A loop of up to `llm.tool_loop_max_iterations` model turns kept the list it resolved at the top. `_run_loop` now treats a committed fold (`_compact_context` grew `compacted`) as the boundary and re-resolves through `_resolve_offer` (the same three steps, minus the turn-start side effects) via `session_refresh.refresh_tools`, which fails CLOSED: a resolver that raises withdraws every tool, an empty resolution is a revocation, and either ends the loop with `_TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY` after a `tool_loop_withdrawn` event rather than asking a provider a turn on a stale or empty list. The offer and the executor move together (`_specs_for` rebuilds the specs, the gate map the executor checks `offered` against, and the untrusted set), so a model that still names the withdrawn tool gets `tool_not_allowed` locally. Between folds the registry is not consulted at all — mid-turn tool sets stay stable, which is Hermes's rule too. A `tool_offer_refreshed` event (added/removed/reason) is written only when something moved. 17 mechanism tests (`tests/test_session_refresh.py`, red-proofed by mutation in the parked commit) plus 15 wiring tests (`tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py`); each half was neutered once and shown red (5 tool-half tests, 2 prompt-half tests).
reviews.remaining: **The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates**: the conversation-level commit exists only with `memory.context_compression` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with `llm.tool_loop_enabled` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild `messages[0]`: a persona change reaches the *next* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" is only as true as the MCP manager's registration into ToolRPC is hot, which this slice did not verify. The lineage row stays at `nerva.context-compaction.v1`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. `refresh_tools` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. H298, H671 and H673 cite the same files and are carried needs_review from #1179 (a sibling stream).

reviews.summary: Configured Ollama num_ctx is sent on generate/tool/stream; /api/show model parameters can resolve a cached effective ceiling, ignoring architectural model_info maxima. Shared-history compression clamps to that ceiling, hard threshold cannot exceed 85%, and a Gemini compaction model reserves its concrete cloud output cap including auto=8192. Review repair: effective soft/hard thresholds are normalized together and actual compression target stays below the effective hard trigger, including soft=hard=1 configurations; protected head/tail remains intact. Ollama and LM Studio structured tool turns now retain the provider-reported input/output token counts. Strict count normalization preserves valid answers when usage metadata is absent or malformed. Tool-loop usage accumulates for metering while context anchors replace with the latest request count; unavailable input does not erase a prior anchor. Gemini structured turns now retain inclusive prompt counts and disjoint candidate/thought output counts; explicitly OpenAI-compatible profiles retain standard prompt/completion totals without adding nested breakdowns. Complete context anchors now include Anthropic disjoint input/cache-read/cache-write counts, including cache-only requests, while totals-only mappings count the full prompt once. Billing semantics remain unchanged. Complete non-stream text replies now publish provider usage through closed request-local observers. Non-stream agent gathers retain per-agent measurements and complete-prefix anchors; ToolRuntime remains the single structured-turn reporter. Retries publish only accepted response usage; cancellation and inherited late tasks cannot outlive the observer. Public string/stream signatures and guardrails are unchanged. OpenRouter inherited streaming reports its single complete text request once. Ollama, LM Studio and Anthropic actual streams now publish one measurement only after confirmed completion: literal done=true, usage-only snapshot plus [DONE], or valid start/final cumulative message_delta usage plus message_stop respectively. Errors, interruption, malformed frames/containers and missing final usage do not reuse intermediate counts. Retry state resets, disjoint cache categories and text callbacks remain intact. Gemini streams now retain a terminal response's own validated prompt/candidate/thought counts after clean HTTP exhaustion and response close. Known single-candidate completion or explicit blocked-prompt semantics are required; errors, raw trailers, cancellation, conflicting response identities and nonzero/malformed candidate indices invalidate the whole attempt. Retries remain isolated and answer callbacks are unchanged. Pinned ask jobs now resolve and freeze their model/window before history construction, cap completion, and omit an unrelated prior usage anchor; unchanged default models retain their existing estimate. Ordinary tool turns now also use immutable configured/cached backend capacity forwarded before guardrails; known limits include completion, initial/later transcript, schemas and structured tool-call arguments. Unknown capacity remains estimated rather than discovered. Reasoning integration was reviewed against previously-current grid33165622 evidence: request-shaping refusals/empty controls do not change this row's cache, session or context/usage semantics. Existing focused regressions are retained. Responses completed text/tool turns and validated terminal streams now retain reported input/output usage. Inclusive input totals split cached_tokens once into disjoint uncached input and cache_read; output reasoning detail is not added to output totals. Missing/malformed metadata does not invent counts. Stream errors, incomplete/contradictory terminal items, cancellation or failed close do not publish usage; request-local sinks preserve existing single-publication semantics. The xAI Responses dialect inherits the same strict reported input/output/cache split and complete terminal accounting, while its own completed-response acceptance rechecks reasoning/replay lifetimes. Reasoning token detail is not added twice to output totals. Opaque function replay preserves main-loop provider usage without introducing ciphertext persistence, per-vendor prices or cache discount assumptions. Shared history compression now preplans each actual governed specialist route and its finite or dynamic completion reserve instead of borrowing the router default model. The strictest input budget stages one shared summary; final prompts/routes are revalidated through at most three monotonically tightening passes before a single accepted clock/history publication. Prepared text/SSE dispatch preserves backend/model/session/lifetime identity, policy gates and known-versus-estimated context metadata. Selected Ollama resolves its own context. Usage anchors require matching backend/model, session generation and retained-history digest; unmanaged old anchors are not promoted to exact managed measurements. Existing disabled-compression behavior and direct local auto output remain unchanged.
reviews.remaining: A model with no num_ctx parameter and no operator configuration remains unresolved (server environment/running context is not probed). Fixed image estimates remain incomplete. Gemini usage-only final frames, absent terminal-local counts, unknown terminal semantics and ambiguous multi-candidate streams deliberately remain unreported. Synthesis/compression/background model calls are deliberately outside conversational usage attribution. Cache discounts/write premiums and undocumented vendor-specific usage mappings are not modeled by the new totals-only adapters. No live provider or billing proof. Responses accounting is limited to supported API-key GPT-4.1 and exact xAI Grok4.5/4.6 dialects, not Codex subscription usage or general OpenAI reasoning-model replay. Cache counts do not establish live discounts, prices or physical context occupancy. Actual specialist planning applies to the existing opt-in shared-compression path; disabled/unmanaged callers retain their existing behavior. Unknown capacity remains a conservative planning estimate, not verified provider metadata.

reviews.summary: Read-only jobs doctor reports scheduler stop/pause, missing registrations, missing/invalid/overdue next runs, execution failures and delivery failures. CLI failures exit non-zero. Doctor also checks script paths and no_agent configuration without reading source; persisted jobs remain inspectable when a script disappears. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported.
